title: The last line first
summary: Learn the piece from the back, one line at a time, so every run-through plays into music you already know.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: A row of eight boxes, one for each line of the piece. The bottom three, shaded, are learned first, since this week learns the piece backward, adding one line at a time from the last line toward the start.

steps.title: The last line first
steps.body:
Most pieces are learned from the beginning, so the beginning gets practised most and the ending least. Then you play for people and the ending, the part they remember, is the shakiest.

This week, learn a new piece backwards, or fix the old one the same way.

1. Play only the last line until it is clean, slowly.
2. Add the line before it, and play both. You are always playing into music you already know.
3. Keep adding one line at a time from the back until you reach the start.
4. Play the whole piece once through. The ending will feel like home.

Learning backwards means every run-through gets easier as it goes, not harder. It also cures the strange feeling of knowing the first page and nothing after it.

figure.alt: A row of eight boxes, one for each line of the piece, the bottom three shaded. Each sitting adds one more line above the shaded ones, always joining onto music already known.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: the last line only, until it is clean
Sitting 2: the last two lines, starting from the one before the end
Sitting 3: add lines from the back until the piece is whole
Sitting 4: the whole piece once through twice; the ending is the part you know best
An old piece played once, ending first, then all of it

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the name of the piece, then play it once through, hands in the frame. Slips stay in.
